text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

- The rightwing nationalist Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) harshly criticised the government's decision on fast privatisation of the country's biggest concerns saying this was meant to provide funds to fulfil promises given in the election campaign, ROP said.

- The opposition centrist Union for Freedom (UW) will appeal to the Constitutional Tribunal against a recent government regulation imposing obligatory ZUS social insurance premiums on incomes of employees previously free from social insurance charges, UW board member Jan Krol said.

- The bankrupt Gdansk shipyard's receiver Andrzej Wiercinski will choose between financing construction of five container ships for Germany's Scholler with funds from Zygmunt Solorz, the Polsat television co-owner, or through a bank credit and 17 million zlotys collected in a charity action by Soldarity trade unions.

- Britain's Pilkington Sandoglass floated glass maker will invest 100 million zlotys in construction of a new plant in Sandomierz, southeastern Poland, in July this year. The firm will eventually employ 300 workers, Sandomierz mayor Wieslaw Warzecha said.

- The agent representing the Greek vessel Thelisis will be fined $12,000 for contamination of the Oder river with oil-related chemicals in the area of Szczecin, northwestern Poland, Szcecin port authorities said.
- Local government officials of Poland's Szczecin and Germany's Barnim municipaities attended a seminar on cooperation on tourist infrastructure and service development in the two border regions.
- Around 100 sanitary engineering, heating and air-conditioning firms exhibited their products at the Eco-Energy-Expo fair in Bydgoszcz, western Poland, last week.

- The Szczecin shipyard would like to take a controlling stake in Gdynia shipyard as soon as possible but the Gdynia yard's general shareholders meeting decided to offer the stake to all interested investors rather than just Szczecin.

- The Centertel mobile phone firm controlled by Telekomunikacja Polska SA, the state telecoms monopolist, will be allowed to tender for launching a DCS-1800 mobile phone network, while the two existing GSM operators were denied the right to tender this time, the telecommunications ministry said.

- The Swarzedzkie Fabryki Mebli (SFM) furniture maker will sign an agreement today with 11 creditor banks to convert 50 percent of its 60 million zlotys liabilities to shares, pass it to the banks, and repay the rest of the debts in the next four years, SFM said.

- Wrong selection of companies and a lack of transparency of information about controlled firms were the cardinal sins of Poland's National Investment Funds (NFI), according to "A Piece of Poland", a report recently published by Merrill Lynch.

NOTE - Dziennik Prawa i Gospordarki is a new daily which combines the former Nowa Europa business daily and Gazeta Prawna, a legal publication which appeared twice weekly. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
